subject: science
title: Gifts From Earth
about: Natural resources and how people use them: trees, soil, water, clay, metal, oil, coal, plants and animals (ESS.1.3.1). Also that resources are not found everywhere.
tip: At dinner, pick one thing on the table and trace it back: the glass came from sand, the fork from metal in the ground.

cards.note: Paper is made from wood. Wood comes from trees.

cards.q: What do we grow our food in?
cards.note: Soil gives plants water and nutrients.

cards.q: What are bricks and flower pots made from?
cards.note: Clay is soft, sticky earth. It gets hard when it is baked.

cards.q: Most cars burn gas. What is gas made from?
cards.note: Oil comes from deep in the ground.

cards.q: Where does our drinking water come from?
cards.note: Some drinking water also comes from wells deep in the ground.

cards.q: What are metal pots and pans made from?
cards.note: Metal is found inside rocks in the ground.

cards.q: Where do the fish we eat come from?
cards.note: Fish are a food that comes from water.

cards.q: Where do natural resources come from?
cards.note: A natural resource is something from Earth that people use.

cards.q: Where do wool, milk and eggs come from?
cards.note: Wool comes from sheep, milk from cows and eggs from hens.

cards.q: Where does the cotton in a shirt come from?
cards.note: Cotton grows in soft white puffs on a cotton plant.

cards.q: What do people melt to make glass?
cards.note: Sand gets so hot it melts. Then it cools into clear glass.

cards.q: People burn coal and oil. What does that make?
cards.note: Some power plants burn coal to make electricity for our homes.

cards.q: A desert has lots of sand. What does it have very little of?
cards.note: Natural resources are not found everywhere. A desert has very little water.

cards.q: What do people build with rocks and stone?
cards.note: Stone is strong. Stone walls can stand for hundreds of years.

cards.q: Where can the salt for our food come from?
cards.note: Salt also comes from salt rock in the ground.
